full_judgment:
Obaidul Hassan J: By this application under section 439 read with section 435 of the Code of Criminal Procedure,1898 the accused petitioner has challenged the legality and propriety of order dated 20-9-2018 passed by the learned Special Judge, Court No. 6, Dhaka in Special Case No. 11 of 2018 (Metro Special Case No. 65 of 2008; Special Case No.12 of 2008), arising out of Gulshan Police Station Case No. 47(9)07 dated 16-9-2007 corresponding to ACC GR No. 99 of 2007 under sections 26(2) and 27(1) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 disposing of all three applications filed by the petitioner on 20-9-2018. 

 2. Facts in short are that, the petitioner is the sole accused in above Special Case No. 11 of 2018 under sections 26(2) and 27(1) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 for allegedly giving false statement of assets and keeping in possession properties disproportionate to his known source of income. On 21-6-2017 the learned Special Judge, Court No. 6, Dhaka framed charge against the petitioner in above case under sections 26(2) and 27(1) of the Anti-Corruption Commission Act, 2004 and fixed the case for recording of evidence. 

 3. The petitioner instituted Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 32982 of 2017 for transfer of above case from above mentioned 6th Court of Special Judge, Dhaka and a Bench of the High Court Division allowed the above Miscellaneous Case and transferred the Special Case from 6th Court of Special Judge, Dhaka to the Metropolitan Senior Special Judge and Dhaka for trial. 

 4. Above court fixed the case on 25-3-2018 for recording of evidence. On above date the petitioner filed a petition under section 94 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for calling for some documents including the documents seized from the law chamber of the accused petitioner at 125/A, Motijheel Commercial Area on 13-4-2007 while he was in prison. A hand written seizure list of above documents was provided to the petitioner through his lawyer pursuant to an order passed in Writ Petition No. 6302 of 2007. In above writ petition the High Court Division has given an order for providing the petitioner an opportunity to peruse the original seized documents (Annexure-A1) before the trial, if any, begins. The learned Metropolitan Senior Special Judge, Dhaka was pleased to allow the petition dated 25-3-2018 in part and directed the Investigation Officer to produce above documents. 

 5. Pursuant to above order the Investigating Officer has made available to the petitioner copies of all prosecution documents of Special Case No. 11 of 2018, but did not make available the documents seized from the law chamber of the petitioner on 13-4-2007 (Annexure-A1). As such the petitioner again filed a petition before the Special Judge, Court No. 6, Dhaka on 20-9-2018 for documents as mentioned in the order of Writ Petition No. 6302 of 2007 (Annexure-A) but the learned Judge disposed of the petition holding that pursuant to order No. 111 dated 24-4-2018 of the Metropolitan Senior Special Judge, Dhaka all documents and alamats of this case have been made available to the accused petitioner. Hence, this petition. 

 8. On the other hand, Mr Khurshid Alam Khan, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the Anti-Corruption Commission stated that the Special Case No. 11 of 2018 has no connection with the above mentioned documents seized from the law chamber of the petitioner on 13-4-2003 (Annexure-A1). This case was neither instituted on the basis of above documents nor the prosecution intends to use those documents in evidence in this case. In fact ACC does not have any knowledge about above seized documents since it did not conduct the alleged search and seizure nor those documents are in the possession of the ACC. As such, pursuant to order dated 20-9-2018 the Investigating officer of the ACC has made available to the petitioner all documents and alamats of Special Case No. 11 of 2018. 

 10. In reply to a query Mr Moudud Ahmed has frankly conceded that the petitioner was given access to all documents and alamats of Special Case No. 11 of 2018. It was also conceded that the documents seized from the chamber of the petitioner on 13-4-2007 do not form part of the record of Special Case No. 11 of 2018. 

 11. It turns out from the seizure list dated 14-4-2007 (Annexure-A1) that the same was prepared by a Sub Inspector of Motijheel Police Station on 14-4-2007 in connection with Motijheel PS Kilo CC No.1580 dated 13-4-2007. Above search or seizure was not conducted by the Anti-Corruption Commission nor those were done in connection this this case. 

 13. It is Cristal clear from above order that the same is about above seized documents and the High Court Division viewed that if any trial begins of any case involving above seized documents then before the trial the petitioner be given an opportunity to peruse the original documents. 

 14. We have found that the above seizure was not made by ACC nor this case has been instituted utilizing above seized documents. Above documents is not part of the record of this case. As such there is no relevance of the direction passed in Writ Petition No. 6302 of 2007 with this case in hand. 

 15. Any person made an accused in a criminal case has an indefinable right to get access to all documents of the case before trial of the same begins. As mentioned above the accused has already got access to all prosecution documents of this case. The documents seized from the law chamber on 14-7-2007 do not form part of this case; those are outside of the case record. 

 16. An accused may resort to section 94 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for calling for such extraneous documents which are not part of the case record provided that the same is indispensible for the defence of the accused and the same is not legally obtainable. But this right is available only after the closure of prosecution evidence and examination of the accused under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure. 

 19. Since in this case the prosecution evidence has not been completed and the accused has not been examined under section 342 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, we are of the view that the petition filed by the petitioner on 25-3-2018 under section 94 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for calling for documents beyond the case record is premature and misconceived.
